scenes.line1: Can you trust your A/B test results?
scenes.say: Think your A/B test is bulletproof? Let's see what can trip you up.

rows.b: Assign users to A or B group
Plan when to stop and analyze

scenes.say: Start by randomizing users, decide your sample size up front, and always set clear stopping rules before you begin.

scenes.label: Peeking
scenes.sub: Checking results early can fool you
scenes.say: Peeking at results before the test ends can make you think you've found a winner when it's just random noise.
Testing more variants increases your chance of a false positive. Ten variants? Way riskier than just one.

scenes.question: Should you peek at A/B test results?
scenes.wrong: Yes, to stop early if it looks good
scenes.right: No, peeking inflates false positives and misleads results
scenes.say: Interview trap: peeking sounds efficient, but it breaks your test and leads to bad decisions.
